title: Eval expected results
description: Ground truth for one repository in the eval corpus: the acceptable verdict(s) for each check the scorer (tools/eval/score.py) checks a headless audit run against. Hand-written, or derived from the deterministic engine's own report and then corrected by a person (DP S11, review R-07). Pinned to one commit so repeat runs are comparable. Rules a schema cannot express are in SCHEMA.md.

expected_version.description: Version of this schema. 0.x versions may break between releases.

repo_label.description: The repository's short label, matching the audit report's own repo_label for the same run.

repo_sha.description: The commit this file's ground truth was written against. A run against a different commit is not comparable; the scorer records the mismatch rather than silently comparing anyway.

notes.description: Free text about the repository: why it is in the corpus, and what it is meant to exercise (a fixture's known single defect, a real repo's particular mix of ecosystems, a planted-injection test, and so on).

checks.description: One entry per check the corpus has ground truth for. A check this array is silent on is not scored for this repository; the scorer neither credits nor penalises it.

id.description: A check ID from the catalogue, for example EXEC-02.

acceptable_verdicts.description: Any verdict in this list scores as a match. More than one acceptable verdict says the ground truth itself is not sharper than that — for example an ecosystem the engine can legitimately read as either PARTIAL or FAIL depending on exactly what it finds.

required_evidence_paths.description: Paths that must appear in this check's evidence for a run to count as right for the right reason, not just the right verdict by coincidence. Absent or empty means only the verdict is scored.

notes.description: Why this is the ground truth: what a person found and confirmed, and anything a scorer or reader should know before disputing it.
